questions.question: What is the chemical name of Marble?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Calcium carbonate**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Calcium carbonate

 
 
• Calcium carbonate, often known as CaCO3, may be found in almost every part of the planet and accounts for more than 4% of the crust of the earth.
 
• Chalk, limestone, and marble are their most prevalent forms in nature.
 
• These three stones were formed over the course of millions of years by the sedimentation of the fossilized shells of small fossilized snails, shellfish, and coral.
 
• Although there is no difference between any of the three forms in terms of their chemical composition, there are other ways in which they are distinct from one another, including purity, whiteness, thickness, and homogeneity.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Calcium oxide**

 
 
• CaO is the chemical formula for calcium oxide.
 
• Calcium and oxygen are the two primary elements that makeup calcium oxide.
 
• In order to make it, calcium carbonate (like limestone) is heated to temperatures between 500 and 600 degrees Celsius in a special kiln called a lime kiln, where it breaks down into oxide and carbon dioxide.
 
 
 
• **Calcium bicarbonate**
 
 
• ​Ca(HCO3)2 is the chemical formula for calcium bicarbonate, which is also known as calcium hydrogen carbonate.
 
• Calcium bicarbonate is often referred to as cleaning lime.
 
• Both sodium bicarbonate and this compound contain bicarbonate, which is composed of hydrogen, carbon, and oxygen atoms.
 
• The formation of caverns, stalagmites, and stalactites results in the production of cleansing lime, which only exists in liquid form.
 
 
 
• **Calcium hydroxide**
 
 
• ​Calcium hydroxide, often known as slaked lime, is represented by the chemical formula Ca(OH)2. 
 
• In its solid form, this inorganic chemical appears white and powdery.
 
• On the other hand, crystallized Ca(OH)2 looks completely colorless.

questions.question: Which RBI tool refers to buying and selling of bonds issued by the Government in the open market?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __Open Market Operations__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Open market operations (OMO) refer to a central bank's buying and selling of government securities in the open market in order to expand or contract the amount of money in the banking system.
 
• Securities purchases inject money into the banking system and stimulate growth, while sales of securities do the opposite and contract the economy.
 
• RBI carries out the OMO through commercial banks and does not directly deal with the public.
 
• OMO is one of the tools that RBI uses to smoothen the liquidity conditions throughout the year and minimize its impact on the interest rate and inflation rate levels.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• RBI was founded on 1 April 1935, in Kolkata.

 
 
• HQ in Mumbai.
 
• Present Governor is** ****Sanjay Malhotra.**
 
• The RBI is responsible for implementing monetary and credit policies, issuing currency notes, being a banker to the government, a regulator of the banking system, manager of foreign exchange, and regulator of payment & settlement systems while continuously working towards the development of Indian financial markets.
 
• RBI is not a Commercial Bank.
 
• RBI was nationalized on 1st January 1949.

questions.question: After which war, Ashoka abandoned the policy of physical occupation?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Kalinga War**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Kalinga War**

 
 
• Ashoka is considered one of the greatest rulers of Indian history who ruled between 273BC to 232BC.
 
• The Kalinga war was fought in 261BC which was the turning event of his life.
 
• The war caused large-scale destruction where 1,00,000 soldiers and civilians were killed.
 
• After the war, Ashoka renounced violence and embraced Ahimsa, the teaching of Buddha.
 
• He implemented the principles of Ahimsa in his empire and spread Buddhism.
 
• He banned violent sports activity and hunting.
 
• He tried to maintain friendly relations with neighbours and avoided war.
 
• Inspired by buddha he advocated the principles of Dhamma which promoted the morality of the empire.
 
• Thus, it is cleared that after the Kalinga War, Ashoka adopted the Policy of Ahimsa.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] Additional Information__

 
• **Battle of the Hydaspes**

 
 
• Battle of Hydaspes was fought in the year 326 BC.
 
• It was fought between Alexander The Great and King Porus.
 
• It was fought on the Banks of River Jhelum.
 
• Alexander defeated Porus in the battle but restored him his Kingdom.
 
• Alexander stayed in India for 19 months.
 
 
 
• **Battle of the Tarain****​**
 
 
• The First Battle of Tarain was fought between The Ghurids (Muzz-Ad-din Mohammad Ghori) against The Chahamanas on 13th November 1191.
 
• The Ghurids (Muzz-Ad-din Mohammad Ghori) were represented by Mu'izz-Ad-Din Mohammad Ghori's Army and The Chahamanana was represented by Prithviraj Chauhan.
 
• The First Battle of Tarain was fought at Tarain presently (Taraori, Haryana).
 
• The Ghurids king (Mu'izz-Ad-Din Mohammad Ghori) and his Army captured the Tabarhindah Fort (Presently Bathinda), which was presumably under The Chahamana's control.
 
• In 1191, Prithviraj Chauhan marched against The Ghurids (Ghori's) Army when he got the news of the Invasion of The Ghurids Army he moved with his Infantry, Cavalry force, and an Elephant Force.
 
 
 
• **Magadha - Anga war**
 
 
• Magadha came into prominence under the** leadership of ****Bimbisara**.
 
• He had a rivalry With Avanti king Pradyota, but later became friends.
 
• Bimbsara even sent his royal physician** Jivaka to Ujjain**, when Pradyota had jaundice.
 
• The most notable conquest by Bimbisara was that of** Anga**.

questions.question: Which among the following planets is also known as Earth's twin?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Venus**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Venus: 

 
 
• Venus is Earth's twin in size.
 
• Venus is the hottest planet in our solar system.
 
• It is the brightest planet in the Solar System.
 
• It is also sometimes referred to as the sister planet to Earth, due to their near similarity of size and mass.
 
• Venus is referred to as the “morning star” and “evening star”.
 
• It is the second planet from the Sun.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Neptune**

 
 
• It is a Bluish-Greenish Planet.
 
• Neptune is the fourth-largest planet in diameter.
 
• In terms of mass, it is 17 times the mass of Earth.
 
• It takes 160 years approximately to orbit around the sun.
 
• Its atmosphere comprises hydrogen and helium.
 
• The absorption of red light by the atmosphere due to the trace amount of Methane gives this planet a greenish-blue to hue colour. 
 
 
 
• Jupiter:
 
 
• Jupiter is the planet, **orange **in color with white bands on it.
 
• Jupiter is the** largest planet **in the **Solar System**.
 
• Jupiter's atmosphere is mostly made up of hydrogen (**H2**) and helium (**He**).
 
 
 
• Saturn:
 
 
• Saturn is known most for its **rings**.
 
• It is the **second-largest** planet in our solar system.
 
• Saturn's atmosphere is also mostly made up of hydrogen (**H2**) and helium (**He**).

questions.question: Who was the spiritual guru of Swami vivekananda?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Ramakrishna Paramahansa**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__ **

__
 
• Swami Vivekananda__

 __
 
• He was influenced by **Ramakrishna Paramhamsa** who became his Guru.
 
• He became a monk and traveled all over India and the West.
 
• He established many Mathas in India the most important being the **Belur Math in Belur**, Howrah district.
 
• He founded the Ramakrishna Mission in May **1897**.
 
• He is best known in the United States for his groundbreaking speech to the** 1893 **World’s Parliament of Religions in which he introduced Hinduism to America and called for religious tolerance and an end to fanaticism.
 
• Narendranath Datta, often known as Swami Vivekananda, was an Indian Hindu monk, philosopher, and writer.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Gopal Krishna Gokhale**

 
 
• In 1905, Gopal Krishna Gokhale founded 'Servants of India Society'. 
 
• The Servants of India Society was formed in Pune on June 12, 1905, for the expansion of Indian education.
 
• Servants of India Society's aim was to unite and train Indians of different ethnicities and religions in welfare work.
 
• It was the first secular organization in that country to devote itself to the underprivileged, rural and tribal people, and other social causes.
 
• Members go through a five-year training period and agree to serve on extremely modest salaries.
 
 

 
• **Acharya Narendra Dev**

 
 
• Acharya Narendra Dev, who was born on __October 31, 1889, in a lawyer’s family in Sitapur in Uttar Pradesh.
 
• Acharya Narendra Dev was the person who remained a member of the All India Congress Committee (AICC) from 1916 to 1948 and who was one of the foremost socialist leaders, Buddhist scholars, and educationists of the country. 
 
• Narendra Dev spent his formative years in Faizabad, the twin town of Ayodhya, and attended the Lucknow session of the Congress with his father in 1899 when he was only ten years old.

questions.question: Agra Fort is one of the popular Mughal monuments built in the 16th century by ________
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Akbar**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Agra Fort 

 
 
• It is located on the right bank of the Yamuna River in the historical city of Agra in Uttar Pradesh.
 
• This grand structure was built by the Mughal emperor Akbar in the year 1573.
 
• The structure displays the architectural grandeur of the Mughal dynasty in India.
 
• The fort complex was assigned a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 1983.
 
 
 
• **Akbar period architecture**
 
 
• Buland Darwaza
 
• Tomb of Shesh Salim Chishti
 
• Panch Mahal
 
• Palace of Jodhabai or Mariam-uz-Zamani
 
• Ibadatkhana
 
• Pachisi Aangan
 
• Hiran Minar
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Shah Jahan**

 
 
• Shahjahan the fifth Mughal emperor of India was the son of Jahangir. His grandfather Akbar gave him the name Khurram.
 
• He was given the title of "The Builder of the Marvels" as he had a remarkable ability to design new structures and redesign old forts.
 
• He built the Taj Mahal in Agra, the Moti Masjid in Lahore, the Jama Masjid of Delhi, and a Section of Agra Fort, etc.**​**
 
 
 
• Humayun (1530 to 1540 and again from 1555 to 1556)
 
 
• Babur's son Humayun ascended the throne of India three days after Babur's death in 1530.
 
• Six months after his accession, Humayun besieged the fortress of Kalinjar in Bundelkhand.
 
• And gained a decisive victory over Afghans at Douhrua and drove out Mahmood Lodi and even defeated Bahadur Shah of Gujarat.
 
• Humayun forces were defeated by Afghan ruler Sher Shah Suri at Chausa near Buxar in June 1539.
 
• On May 17, 1540, the Mughals and the Afghans met again opposite Kannauj.
 
• His hopelessly demoralised army was defeated at the battle commonly known as the Battle of Kannauj.
 
• Humayun captured **Rohtas Fort and** **Lahore **in February **1555**. 
 
 
 
• Babur
 
 
• Babur was born in 1483 in Andijan, which is now Uzbekistan.
 
• His father was the ruler of the small kingdom of Ferghana in Central Asia.
 
• When Babur was 11 years old, his father died, and he became the ruler of Ferghana.
 
• However, he was soon driven out of his kingdom by his enemies, and he spent the next few years wandering in Central Asia and trying to regain his throne.
 
• Babur finally succeeded in regaining Ferghana in 1494 when he was 12 years old.

questions.question: Pradhan Mantri Gramodaya Yojana was launched in ______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**2000**__. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The Pradhan Mantri Gramodaya Yojana (PMGY) was launched by the Indian government in the year 2000.
 
• This scheme was initiated to focus on the village development in five critical areas - primary health, primary education, housing, rural roads, and drinking water.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The primary objective of PMGY is to achieve the goal of sustainable human development at the village level.
 
• Primary Health: The scheme provides for health centers and necessary healthcare infrastructure at the village level. 
 
• Primary Education: Under PMGY, the government allocates resources for strengthening the primary education system in rural areas, including the establishment of new schools and providing necessary infrastructure and learning materials.
 
• Housing: PMGY also aims to improve the housing condition of the rural poor.
 
• Rural Roads: PMGY recognizes the importance of connectivity for the overall development of villages.
 
• Drinking Water: Under the scheme, the government provides resources to ensure the supply of safe and clean drinking water to the rural population.
 
• The funds for this centrally sponsored scheme are shared between the central government and the states. 
 
• The success of PMGY depends on the active participation of the community in the planning and implementation of the programs.

questions.question: The constituent assembly was formed on the recommendation of the Cabinet Mission which visited India in______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**1946**__. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The Constituent Assembly of India was formed on the recommendations of the Cabinet Mission which visited India in **1946.**
 
• **The Cabinet Mission,** consisting of members from the **British government**, aimed to discuss and negotiate the terms of the** transfer of power from the British Raj to the Indian leadership.**
 
• The Mission proposed the formation of an interim government and a constituent assembly to frame the **Constitution of India.​**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• This assembly was formed from elected representatives of the provinces of India and nominated members from the princely states.
 
• The first meeting of the Constituent Assembly was held in **December 1946, with Dr. Sachchidananda Sinha as the interim President.**
 
• Later, Dr. Rajendra Prasad was elected as the President of the Constituent Assembly.
 
• The Assembly took almost three years to complete its historic task of drafting the Constitution for Independent India.
 
• **On 26th November 1949**, the Constitution was adopted, and it came into force on the **26th of January, 1950 **marking the beginning of a new era in the history of India.

questions.question: The Competition (Amendment) Bill, 2022 aims to regulate mergers and acquisitions based on the value of transactions, and says that deals with transaction value of more than Rs. 2,000 crore will require the Competition Commission of India's approval, For faster approvals, the proposed las also says the timeline for CCI to pass an order on such transactions will be reduced to _______ days from 210 days.
questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**150**__. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Recently, the Competition (Amendment) Bill, 2022, which seeks to amend the Competition Act, 2002, was passed in the Lower House amid protests from the Opposition.
 
• And the Forest (Conservation) Amendment Bill, 2023 is also introduced in parliament.
 
• For faster approvals, the proposed las also says the timeline for CCI to pass an order on such transactions will be reduced to 150 days from 210 days.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **The Competition Act of 2002** was established to oversee and maintain competition within the Indian marketplace, and it explicitly forbids anti-competitive conduct such as cartels, misuse of a dominant market position, and mergers and acquisitions that might negatively impact competition. 
 
• This Act was later modified by the **Competition (Amendment) Act of 2007.**
 
• The duty of implementing and enforcing the Act falls under the purview of the **Competition Commission of India (CCI).**
 
• The Competition Appellate Tribunal, a legal body formed under the auspices of the **Competition Act of 2002,** is authorized to review and adjudicate on appeals against any decisions, rules, or orders issued by the **CCI.**
 
• However, in **2017, the government replaced the Competition Appellate Tribunal with the National Company Law Appellate Tribunal (NCLAT), which now carries out the functions previously performed by the former.****​**

questions.question: Which among the following acts introduced the Diarchy, i.e,, rule of two which means executive councillors and popular ministers?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Montague-Chelmsford Reform (Government of India Act), 1919**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **The system of Diarchy, which means dual government consisting of executive councilors and popular ministers.**
 
• It** **was introduced in the provinces of British India through the Montague-Chelmsford Reforms, which were incorporated in the **Government of India Act, 1919. **
 
• **Under this system**, the provincial subjects of administration were divided into two categories - 'transferred' and 'reserved'.
 
• The transferred subjects were to be administered by the Governor.
 
• This marked a significant step towards the establishment of responsible government in India.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Charter Act, 1813:**

 
 
• This Act was passed by the **British Parliament to renew the charter of the East India Company**
 
• **The 1813 Act** marked a significant shift, however, as it ended the Company's monopoly over Indian trade, except for trade in tea and trade with China.
 
• The Act also made p**rovision for spending one lakh rupees annually for education in India.**
 
 
 
• **Government of India Act, 1858:**
 
 
• This Act was enacted in the wake of the **1857 Revolt in India.**
 
• It abolished the **East India Company** and transferred the administration of India directly to the British Crown.
 
• The British monarch's representative, the Governor-General of India, was given extensive powers.
 
 
 
• **Indian Council Act, 1861:**
 
 
• This Act is known for** initiating the process of decentralisation in India.**
 
• It restored the legislative powers to the Bombay and Madras Presidencies.
 
• It provided for the establishment of new legislative councils for** Bengal, North-West Frontier Province, and Punjab.**

questions.question: Balanoglossus belongs to which of the following phylum of animal kingdom?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Hemichordata**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Hemichordata: **

 
 
• This phylum includes marine worm-like creatures, such as acorn worms (like Balanoglossus) and graptolites.
 
• Hemichordates are characterized by pharyngeal slits, similar to those of chordates, and a structure known as a stomochord in the collar, which is similar to the notochord in chordates.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Arthropoda: **

 
 
• This is the largest phylum in the animal kingdom and includes creatures like insects, spiders, and crustaceans.
 
• Arthropods are characterized by their jointed legs (the word "arthropoda" means "jointed feet" in Greek) and a hard exoskeleton made of chitin.
 
 
 
• **Echinodermata:**
 
 
• This phylum includes marine animals like starfish, sea urchins, and sea cucumbers.
 
• Echinoderms are characterized by radial symmetry, spiny skin, and a water vascular system that aids in locomotion, feeding, and respiration.
 
 
 
• **Mollusca:**
 
 
• This is one of the most diverse phyla and includes animals like snails, octopuses, and clams.
 
• Molluscs are characterized by a soft body, which in many species is protected by a hard shell, and a muscular 'foot' used for movement.

questions.question: Which among the following is a subject of Union Lists in Constitution of India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Extradition**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **subject among the given options that fall under the Union List in the Constitution of India is Extradition**
 
• In the Constitution of India, the** seventh schedule classifies the subjects of legislation into three lists: Union, State, and Concurrent.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The **Seventh Schedule** of the Indian constitution gives allocation of powers and functions between the **Union & States.**
 
• **It contains 3 lists:**

 
• Union List (For central Govt) 100 Subjects (originally 97).
 
• States List (Powers of State Govt) 61 subjects (originally 66). 
 
• Concurrent List (Both Union & States) 52 subjects (originally 47).

 
• **Union List: Union Legislature alone can make laws on these matters.**

 
 
• Defence
 
• Atomic Energy
 
• Foreign Affairs
 
• War and Peace
 
• Banking
 
• Railways
 
• Post and Telegraph
 
• Airways
 
• Ports
 
• Foreign Trade
 
• Currency & Coinage
 
 
 
• **State List: State Legislature can make laws on these matters (though it sometimes has exceptions).**
 
 
• Agriculture
 
• Police
 
• Prison
 
• Local Government
 
• Public Health
 
• Land
 
• Liquor
 
• Trade and Commerce
 
• Livestock and Animal Husbandry
 
• State Public Services
 
 
 
• **Concurrent List: Both Union and State Legislature alone can make laws on these matters. **
 
 
• Education
 
• Transfer of Property other than Agricultural land
 
• Forests
 
• Trade Unions
 
• Adulteration
 
• Adoption and Succession

questions.question: Union Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman announced in 2022 that she will launch the _______ platform which is an online learning platform for Oriental and South Asian Studies.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Bharat Vidya**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• **Union Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman** has announced the launch of **Bharat Vidya, an online learning platform for Oriental and South Asian Studies.**
 
• The platform is designed and developed by the **Bhandarkar Oriental Research Institute (BORI).**
 
• **Bharat Vidya will offer both free and paid courses covering various aspects** of Indology **including art, architecture, philosophy, language, and science.**
 
• Initially, the platform will offer six courses: **Veda Vidya, Bharatiya Darshanshastra, Sanskrit learning, 18 Parvas of Mahabharata, Fundamentals of Archaeology, and Kalidasa and Bhasha.**
 
• BORI will work in collaboration with **Indian and foreign universities to award credits for its courses.**
 
• The courses on the Bharat Vidya platform are in line with the **New Education Policy (NEP) 2020, as announced by Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman during the inaugural event.**
 
• The platform, **Bharat Vidya, is the first of its kind dedicated to Oriental and South Asian studies.**
 
• In addition to the **Bharat Vidya, Bank Maha Pack also includes Live Batches, Test Series, Video Lectures & eBooks.**
